svg.title: VFR fuel reserve: 30 minutes by day, 45 minutes at night
svg.desc: 14 CFR 91.151. Before beginning a flight in an airplane under VFR you need enough fuel, considering wind and forecast weather, to reach the first point of intended landing and then, at normal cruising speed, to fly at least 30 minutes by day or at least 45 minutes at night. Two bars show trip fuel followed by the reserve, longer at night. Rotorcraft need 20 minutes.
svg.text: Fuel to reach the first point of intended landing, then a reserve at normal cruising speed. It is a minimum.
Fuel to the first landing point
Fuel to the first landing point
Fuel to the first landing point is figured considering wind and forecast weather.
Reserve: flying time at normal cruising speed, after the first point of intended landing.
Reserve bars are drawn to scale with each other: 30 minutes against 45.
reserve gallons = reserve minutes ÷ 60 × gallons per hour at normal cruise
It is the fuel you need before you begin the flight
Rotorcraft (such as helicopters) need 20 minutes (91.151(b)); the bars above are for airplanes.
Many pilots plan more than this minimum; your instructor can tell you what they plan for your airplane.
